items.ex: 이 옷이 저 옷보다 훨씬 예뻐요.

bg-32-01.hint: Today is much warmer than yesterday.
bg-32-01.why: Comparative standard takes -보다: 어제보다 훨씬 따뜻해요.

bg-32-01.q: Write a sentence comparing today and yesterday's weather using 어제보다 and 따뜻해요.
bg-32-01.why: 어제 is the comparison standard taking -보다.

a.d: Attached to the standard of comparison to indicate that something has more or less of a quality.
ex: 기차가 버스**보다** 빨라요. — The train is faster than the bus.

b.d: Attached to a noun to show similarity or resemblance in appearance, action, or manner.
ex: 아이**처럼** 웃어요. — Smiles like a child.

bg-32-01.tip: Use -보다 for differences (better, faster, bigger) and -처럼 for likeness (acting or looking like something).

steps.en: Today the weather is much warmer than yesterday.

ko: 봄이 되어서 날씨가 어제보다 훨씬 따뜻해졌어요.
공원에 나가니 아이들이 나비처럼 즐겁게 뛰어놀고 있었어요.
오랜만에 따뜻한 햇살을 받으며 산책하니 기분이 아주 상쾌했어요.
en: Spring arrived, so the weather became much warmer than yesterday.
Going out to the park, children were running and playing happily like butterflies.
Walking while receiving warm sunlight after a long time, I felt very refreshed.

bg-32-01.q: How is the weather today compared to yesterday?
How were the children playing in the park?
bg-32-01.why: The text states '나비처럼 즐겁게 뛰어놀고 있었어요'.

items: I can compare two things using the particle -보다.
I can describe similarities or metaphors using -처럼.

bg-32-02.hint: I work from Monday to Friday.
bg-32-02.why: Time range starting point takes -부터 and endpoint takes -까지.

bg-32-02.q: Write a sentence saying lunch time is from 12 to 1 o'clock using 12시부터 and 1시까지.
bg-32-02.why: 12시 is the starting time (-부터) and 1시 is the ending time (-까지).

steps.en: I study from morning until evening.
At the library from morning until evening, I study hard.

ko: 저는 평일에 회사에서 월요일부터 금요일까지 근무해요.
매일 오전 아홉 시부터 오후 여섯 시까지 일하고 퇴근해요.
주말에는 일을 쉬고 집에서 편안하게 휴식을 취해요.
en: On weekdays, I work at the company from Monday to Friday.
Every day I work from 9 AM to 6 PM and leave work.
On weekends I take a break from work and relax comfortably at home.

bg-32-02.q: Which days does the writer work?
What does the writer do on weekends?
bg-32-02.why: The text says '주말에는 일을 쉬고 집에서 편안하게 휴식을 취해요'.

items: I can set time and date boundaries using -부터 (from) and -까지 (until).
I can describe weekly schedules and operating hours naturally.

bg-32-03.hint: I have only 1,000 won in my wallet.
bg-32-03.why: -밖에 strictly requires a negative ending predicate like 없어요: 천 원밖에 없어요.

bg-32-03.q: Write a sentence saying you only drank water using 물만 and 마셨어요.
bg-32-03.why: With the affirmative verb 마셨어요, you must use -만 instead of -밖에.

a.d: Can be used with either positive or negative verbs to state a simple focus or limitation.
ex: 사과**만** 있어요. — There are only apples.

b.d: MUST be followed by a negative verb (없어요, 안 해요, 못 가요) to emphasize insufficiency or lack.
ex: 사과**밖에** 없어요. — There is nothing but apples.

bg-32-03.tip: Never say 밖에 있어요 (incorrect!). Always pair -밖에 with 없어요, 안, or 못.

steps.en: In my wallet, there is only 1,000 won.
Right now in my wallet, only 1,000 won remains.

ko: 기차 출발 시간까지 십 분밖에 안 남았어요.
편의점에 들를 시간이 없어서 자판기에서 물만 얼른 샀어요.
서둘러 달려서 기차를 놓치지 않고 무사히 탔어요.
en: There are only ten minutes left until the train departs.
Since there was no time to drop by a convenience store, I quickly bought only water from a vending machine.
Running in a hurry, I safely boarded the train without missing it.

bg-32-03.q: How much time was left until train departure?
bg-32-03.why: The text says '십 분밖에 안 남았어요'.

bg-32-03.q: What did the writer buy at the vending machine?
bg-32-03.why: The text says '자판기에서 물만 얼른 샀어요'.

items: I can express limitation using -만 with affirmative verbs.
I can emphasize scarcity or shortage using -밖에 strictly with negative endings.

bg-32-04.hint: I have only 3,000 won in cash on hand.
bg-32-04.why: Insufficiency with negative predicate 없어요 takes -밖에.

bg-32-04.q: Write a sentence saying you sing well like a singer using 가수처럼 and 노래해요.
Fix the critical error where 밖에 is incorrectly paired with a positive verb.
bg-32-04.hint: 밖에 cannot be paired with affirmative 있어요! Change to negative 없어요 or use 만.
bg-32-04.why: Negative verb 없어요 must be used with 밖에: 오천 원밖에 없어요 (or 오천 원만 있어요).

a.d: Compares two entities: X is more/less adjective than Y.
ex: 여름**보다** 겨울이 좋아요. — I like winter more than summer.

b.d: Denies everything else except the noun, emphasizing scarcity with negative verbs.
ex: 하나**밖에** 없어요. — There is only one left.

bg-32-04.tip: -보다 sets a relative comparison; -밖에 strictly excludes everything else under negative verbs.

base.en: It is more expensive than other clothes.

steps.en: This clothing is more expensive than other clothes.
This clothing at the department store is a little more expensive than other clothes.

ko: 저는 비행기보다 기차 여행을 더 좋아해요.
창밖으로 보이는 풍경이 한 폭의 그림처럼 정말 아름다워요.
시간이 반나절밖에 안 걸려서 주말 여행으로 아주 좋아요.
en: I like train travel more than airplane travel.
The scenery visible outside the window is truly beautiful like a picture.
It takes only half a day, so it is great for a weekend trip.

bg-32-04.q: Which travel method does the writer like more?
bg-32-04.why: The text states '비행기보다 기차 여행을 더 좋아해요'.

bg-32-04.q: What does the scenery look like?
bg-32-04.why: The text says '한 폭의 그림처럼 정말 아름다워요'.

items: I can compare items with -보다 and express poetic similarity with -처럼.
I can properly use -만 and -밖에 to describe limits without grammatical errors.
